text:
mira: heads-up: onboarding sample app (node) showed email leaking after our auth retry path. looks like two different reqids for one user flow. repro below.

oliver: yikes. paste the raw log lines and the sdk init?

mira: sanitized lines:
```
INFO 2026-03-23T12:04:01Z req_id=xyz789 user=carol@example.com event=auth.start
INFO 2026-03-23T12:04:02Z req_id=xyz789 event=auth.retry attempt=1
WARN 2026-03-23T12:04:03Z req_id=zzz000 user=carol@example.com event=auth.finish
```
first two look redacted OK, last one leaked email and has a different req_id. sdk init:
```
SDK.telemetry({ hooks: [attachSpanHook, samplingHook, redactHook] })
```
app stack: express -> retry-mw (re-dispatch) -> sdk.log. suspect retry-mw emits new context.

rachel: is redactHook synchronous? if retry replays the handler it might bypass the redact if hook only runs on span start.

tom: i've seen this before when the library registers redact on span.attach instead of on log.emit. solution was to run redact as the last step on the final record.

mira: tried a tiny patch in sample app:
```
logger.on('flush', (rec) => { if (!rec._redacted) { redactPII(rec); rec._redacted = true } });
```
that fixed the leak locally.

oliver: perf concern though if every emit runs redact. can we short-circuit for records already redacted or for internal spans? marking helps.

telemetry-bot: created ticket DE-5201: "node sdk: retry path causes duplicate req_id + missed redaction" - https://jira/redwood/DE-5201

rachel: also add an integration test that simulates express retry-mw re-dispatch and asserts single stable req_id and no PII in logs.

tom: agree. here's a small test sketch:
```js
// simulate: request -> retry -> re-dispatch -> logger emits
expect(logs.map(l => l.req_id)).toEqual(['xyz789']);
expect(logs.join('')).not.toMatch(/@example.com/);
```

mira: note: mobile/native shims register hooks on the output pipeline so they weren't affected in our quick check. only node express retry re-dispatch pattern.

oliver: plan: (1) add test, (2) change redactHook to run at emit stage by default, (3) add cheap marker to avoid extra CPU on double emissions, (4) ship 0.12.4-canary + monitor error reports. I'll own the PR.

mira: thanks — assigning DE-5201 to oliver and rachel for tests. :thumbsup:
